chunks.text: An intent to file sets a potential start date (also called an effective date) for your VA benefits. When you notify VA that you intend to file a claim, you may be able to receive retroactive payments covering the period between when you submit your intent to file and when VA approves your claim. You can submit an intent to file for three benefit types: disability compensation, pension benefits, and Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC).
chunks.excerpt: An intent to file sets a potential effective date for your VA benefits, letting you receive retroactive payments between your intent to file and your claim approval.
chunks.sourceTitle: VA - Your Intent to File a VA Claim

chunks.text: You can notify VA of your intent to file online, by phone, or by mail. To submit online, complete an intent to file form (VA Form 21-0966). To submit by phone, call VA at 800-827-1000 (TTY: 711), Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. ET. To submit by mail, download and complete VA Form 21-0966 and mail it to the address listed on the form. After you notify VA of your intent to file, you have one year to complete and file your claim.
chunks.excerpt: Notify VA of your intent to file online, by phone (800-827-1000), or by mail (VA Form 21-0966). You then have one year to complete and file your claim.
chunks.sourceTitle: VA - Your Intent to File a VA Claim
chunks.section: How do I notify VA of my intent to file?

chunks.text: You can file a claim for VA disability compensation in several ways. You can file online now using the disability compensation application. You can file by mail by sending an Application for Disability Compensation and Related Compensation Benefits (VA Form 21-526EZ) to the Department of Veterans Affairs Claims Intake Center. You can file in person by bringing your application to a VA regional office. You can also work with an accredited attorney, claims agent, or Veterans Service Organization (VSO) representative to get help filing your claim.
chunks.excerpt: File a VA disability claim online, by mail (VA Form 21-526EZ), in person at a regional office, or with help from an accredited representative or VSO.
chunks.sourceTitle: VA - How to File a VA Disability Claim
chunks.section: How do I file a claim?

chunks.text: If you plan to file for disability compensation using a paper form, you may want to submit an intent to file form first, which can give you time to gather your evidence while preserving an earlier potential start date. If you file online, you don't need to submit a separate intent to file, because your effective date is set automatically when you start the online application before you submit it. On average, VA takes about 70 days to complete a disability-related claim.
chunks.excerpt: Submit an intent to file first if filing on paper; filing online sets your effective date automatically. VA takes about 70 days on average to complete a disability claim.
chunks.sourceTitle: VA - How to File a VA Disability Claim

chunks.text: Before you apply for VA health care, gather the information you'll need. This includes Social Security numbers for you, your spouse, and your qualified dependents; your military discharge papers (DD214) and service history; insurance card information for all insurance that covers you; and your gross household income from the previous calendar year for you, your spouse, and your dependents. You can apply without reporting your income and expenses, but VA may ask for this information later.
chunks.excerpt: To apply for VA health care, gather Social Security numbers, your DD214 and service history, insurance card information, and your previous-year household income.
chunks.sourceTitle: VA - How to Apply for VA Health Care
chunks.section: What information do I need to apply?

chunks.text: You can apply for VA health care in four ways. You can apply online. You can apply by phone by calling 877-222-8387, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. ET. You can apply by mail by completing an Application for Health Benefits (VA Form 10-10EZ) and sending it to the Health Eligibility Center. You can apply in person by bringing a completed VA Form 10-10EZ to your nearest VA medical center or clinic. VA usually decides on health care applications in less than one week.
chunks.excerpt: Apply for VA health care online, by phone (877-222-8387), by mail (VA Form 10-10EZ), or in person. VA usually decides in less than one week.
chunks.sourceTitle: VA - How to Apply for VA Health Care

chunks.text: Before you apply for VA education benefits, find out if you're eligible, gather the documents and information you'll need, and learn about the benefits you'll get at the school you want to attend using the GI Bill Comparison Tool. To apply you'll generally need your Social Security number, your bank account direct deposit information, your education and military history, and basic information about the school or training facility you want to attend.
chunks.excerpt: Before applying for VA education benefits, check eligibility, gather your documents, and compare schools with the GI Bill Comparison Tool.
chunks.sourceTitle: VA - How to Apply for VA Education Benefits
chunks.section: How do I prepare to apply?

chunks.text: You can apply for VA education benefits online, by mail, or with help. To apply online, use the education benefits application for the Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33), the Montgomery GI Bill Active Duty (Chapter 30), or the Montgomery GI Bill Selected Reserve (Chapter 1606). To apply by mail, complete an Application for VA Education Benefits (VA Form 22-1990) and send it to your regional processing office. You can also work with an accredited representative or Veterans Service Organization. On average, VA takes about 30 days to process education claims.
chunks.excerpt: Apply for the GI Bill online, by mail (VA Form 22-1990), or with help. Options include the Post-9/11 (Ch. 33), Montgomery Active Duty (Ch. 30), and Selected Reserve (Ch. 1606) GI Bills.
chunks.sourceTitle: VA - How to Apply for VA Education Benefits

chunks.text: The DoD SkillBridge program gives transitioning service members the chance to gain valuable civilian work experience through specific industry training, apprenticeships, or internships during their last 180 days of military service. With approval from their unit commander, service members can receive up to 180 days of permissive duty to focus on full-time training with an approved industry partner. SkillBridge connects service members with industry partners for real-world job experience, and gives partners an opportunity to evaluate the service member for future employment.
chunks.excerpt: DoD SkillBridge lets transitioning service members train full-time with civilian industry partners during their last 180 days of service, with unit-commander approval.
